graph.summary: Lithium → Glycogen synthase kinase-3 beta → Catenin beta-1 → apoptotic process → Bipolar Disorder

evidence.snippet: Lithium potently inhibits GSK-3 beta activity (Ki = 2 mM), but is not a general inhibitor of other protein kinases.
evidence.explanation: Lithium directly inhibits GSK-3 beta enzymatic activity.

paper.title: A molecular mechanism for the effect of lithium on development.
paper.journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences of the United States of America

evidence.snippet: the direct inhibition on glycogen synthase kinase 3β
evidence.explanation: Review identifying direct GSK-3 beta inhibition as a mechanism of lithium in bipolar disorder.

paper.title: An Oldie but Goodie: Lithium in the Treatment of Bipolar Disorder through Neuroprotective and Neurotrophic Mechanisms.

evidence.snippet: Glycogen Synthase Kinase 3β (GSK3 β) phosphorylates and degrades catenin via the downstream Wnt signalling pathway
evidence.explanation: GSK-3 beta phosphorylates and degrades beta-catenin; its inhibition stabilizes beta-catenin.

paper.title: Evaluation of wound healing active principles in the transdermal patch formulated with crude bio wastes and plant extracts against GSK-3 beta - an in silico study.

evidence.snippet: lithium chloride inhibited glycogen synthase kinase-3β activation, which on one hand, suppressed downstream CRMP-2/NR2B, thus diminishing the excitotoxic index level; and on the other, stabilized β-catenin
evidence.explanation: GSK-3 beta inhibition by lithium stabilizes beta-catenin.

paper.title: The neuroprotective effect of lithium chloride on cognitive impairment through glycogen synthase kinase-3β inhibition in intracerebral hemorrhage rats.

evidence.snippet: stabilized β-catenin, thus modulating its downstream apoptosis-related factors such as NF-κB, Bcl-2 and Bax
evidence.explanation: Stabilized beta-catenin modulates apoptosis-related factors and is paralleled by decreased neuronal death.

paper.title: The neuroprotective effect of lithium chloride on cognitive impairment through glycogen synthase kinase-3β inhibition in intracerebral hemorrhage rats.

evidence.snippet: Li+'s neuroprotective properties are related to its modulation of nerve growth factors, inflammation, mitochondrial function, oxidative stress, and programmed cell death mechanisms such as autophagy and apoptosis.
evidence.explanation: Apoptotic (programmed cell death) mechanisms underlie the neuroprotective action of lithium relevant to bipolar disorder pathology.

paper.title: Lithium as a Neuroprotective Agent for Bipolar Disorder: An Overview.
